edges.description: Organisms that escape the mucosa enter the bloodstream and disseminate.
Circulating bacteria cross the blood-brain or blood-CSF barrier and reach the cerebrospinal-fluid compartment.
Once streptococci cross the barrier, organisms replicate in the cerebrospinal-fluid and subarachnoid compartments.
Pneumococcal pneumolysin engages astroglial connexin-43 during meningeal invasion.
Streptococcal products stimulate innate receptors and inflammatory proteases, recruiting neutrophils into the CSF.
Astroglial cytotoxicity contributes to the parenchymal and barrier injury of streptococcal CNS disease.
Cytokines and MMP-mediated barrier injury drive edema, vasculitis, cochlear injury, and neuronal damage.
The meningeal inflammatory cytokine response produces fever.
Meningeal inflammation produces the neck stiffness of meningism.
Inflammatory injury extends to the inner ear, producing cochlear damage.
Severe cortical and systemic injury depresses consciousness to coma.
Cochlear injury produces persistent sensorineural hearing loss.

evidence.snippet: In adults presenting with community-acquired acute bacterial meningitis, the sensitivity of the classic triad of fever, neck stiffness, and altered mental status is low, but almost all present with at least two of the four symptoms of headache, fever, neck stiffness, and altered mental status.
